speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your neck and arm pain, can you tell me exactly where the pain starts and which fingers feel numb or weak?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or writing, and is the weakness symmetric in both hands? I also need to know if your symptoms worsen when you look up or extend your neck.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of absent reflexes, fasciculations, and symmetric weakness suggests lower motor neuron involvement rather than simple cervical radiculopathy. REQUEST TEST: EMG_Nerve_Conduction_Study

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG is normal, this rules out motor neuron disease and peripheral neuropathy, pointing toward a central nervous system issue. Do you experience any bladder or bowel dysfunction, such as incontinence or retention?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal EMG, symmetric weakness, and inconsistent condom use, I am concerned about a central nervous system infection or compression. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a syrinx, likely secondary to your previous motor vehicle accident. Do you have any sensory deficits, such as a loss of pain or temperature sensation in your hands or arms?

speaker: Patient
text: Oriented to time, place, and person. Vital signs within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. The clinical picture of a cervical syrinx causing segmental loss of pain and temperature sensation, combined with lower motor neuron signs like fasciculations and absent reflexes, confirms the diagnosis of Syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
